ctx.x: No, his brother George, he, that's all he played was snare drums, something like Remus. You see? Mm-hmm. Well, his brother George, he left away from there and went, uh, live in Morgan City. Mm-hmm. That's where he died, over in Morgan City. Could he play pretty good snare drums? Well, he wasn't much of a snare drum player, but he, he'd fill in on the count of his brother was the leader of the band, Old Man Allen, but he'd always use his brother on the snare drum, you know? Mm-hmm. Remus was about the best snare…
I used to always like Arthur Ogle, you know Arthur Hogan? Huh? You remember Arthur Hogan? Yeah. Ogle, he was good, too. Yeah, yeah. And Alfred Wiggins, they were good. A lot of good ones.

Well, I think, uh, out of all of them drummers growing, I think Contrell was about the best drummer over there. I never saw him. No, he was tall. He died. He used to, he used to age in for war lines. He never bought no drums. All he done went in. War lines and got him a set of drums and go out there and flare them and then he'd sell them. Mm-hmm. He had a set of drums, you could fold them up.
